      Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys: Preview, How to Watch

      By Draft Insider
      October 6, 2026
      Facebook
      X
        Listen to audio version of this article
        Sponsored by
        0:00 / 5:47
        Instaread

        The Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys preview starts with a simple question: can a 0-4 team with an undrafted rookie quarterback finally score touchdowns on a short week? The Bucs are winless for the first time in 13 years after a 17-14 home loss to Green Bay. The Cowboys, 2-2, are coming off a 34-30 win over Houston. Tampa Bay needs this one to stay in the NFC South race, and Dallas can’t afford to stumble against a winless opponent in prime time.

        Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys at a Glance

        Current Form

        Tampa Bay’s problem isn’t effort, it’s finishing. The Bucs have now played 10 straight games decided by one score, and the Green Bay loss ended with a final drive that stalled on protection issues. The defense has been solid, holding a third straight opponent under 300 yards against the Packers, with multiple takeaways for the first time this season. The offense has not reached 30 points in any game and has topped 20 only once, in Week 1.

        Dallas has been looser. The Cowboys opened 1-2 and allowed 82 points in those three games. Against the Texans, Dak Prescott threw for 355 yards, Javonte Williams scored three second-half touchdowns, and Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb from 12 yards with 40 seconds left for the winner. It was a win, but the defense gave up 30 points.

        Key Matchups to Watch

        Jalon Daniels vs. Dallas’ reworked pass rush. Daniels, making his second NFL start, threw for 148 yards and a touchdown against Green Bay and added 55 rushing yards. His mobility is an asset. Dallas has rebuilt its front with Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary, and Tampa Bay’s protection broke down on that last drive Sunday.

        Prescott and Lamb vs. a thinner Bucs secondary. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is sidelined with a rib fracture, and Ifeatu Melifonwu is next up. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) did not practice Monday. Tykee Smith has already pointed to Dallas’ receiving talent as the week’s challenge.

        Javonte Williams vs. the Bucs’ run defense. Williams is coming off a three-touchdown half, and Tampa Bay’s front has been stingy against the run. If the Bucs win early downs, they can force Prescott into obvious passing situations. The Bucs also lean on a three-man backfield rotation of Bucky Irving, Sean Tucker and Kenny Gainwell, which Todd Bowles has said needs to be split three ways.

        Players to Watch

        • Jalon Daniels, QB, Buccaneers: The first undrafted rookie to start at quarterback for Tampa Bay. Turnover-free football would be a good start.
        • Dak Prescott, QB, Cowboys: Coming off a 355-yard game, he faces a secondary missing its best playmaker.
        • CeeDee Lamb, WR, Cowboys: He was a full participant Monday despite a thigh issue, and his late touchdown showed he is still Dallas’ closer.
        • Javonte Williams, RB, Cowboys: The second-half engine against Houston.
        • Cade Otton, TE, Buccaneers: Now third in franchise history in receptions by a tight end, and a dependable target for a young quarterback.
        • Josiah Trotter, LB, Buccaneers: The rookie continues to produce. His knee is a watch item.

        Injury Report

        This is based on Monday’s practice report, which the Bucs said is an estimate because they held a walk-through. Official game designations had not been issued as of Tuesday, so check Wednesday and Thursday’s reports before kickoff.

        How to Watch Buccaneers vs. Cowboys

        • TV/Streaming: Prime Video
        • Mobile (in-market): NFL+
        • Out of market: NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV
        • International: Game Pass International on DAZN
        • International kickoff: 1:15 a.m. BST / 2:15 a.m. CEST on Friday, October 9
        • Radio: WXTB 97.9 FM in Tampa Bay, plus the Buccaneers app and Buccaneers.com

        Buccaneers vs. Cowboys Prediction

        Dallas is the better team, and it has the quarterback, the receiver and the home field. The Bucs’ offense has not produced enough to keep pace, and the loss of Winfield removes the one defender who regularly changes games for them.

        The counterargument is the one-score trend. Ten straight close games suggest Tampa Bay’s defense can keep a lid on things, and Dallas’ own defense has been porous. Still, Daniels will face pressure, and Prescott should find openings against a banged-up secondary.

        Prediction: Cowboys 27, Buccaneers 17. That is a 10-point win, right at the opening number. Lines move on injury news, so check the final spread before drawing any betting conclusions.
